background_notes.fact: When n=0 and E is a nonempty subset of V_0, E=V_0, and euclideanProduct 0 E is exactly the set of vectors in V_1 whose sole coordinate t lies in [0,1].

grounds.reason: V_0 is the singleton empty-coordinate vector space.
N006 explicitly concerns the given nonempty E; the boundary observation uses exactly this stated condition.
With zero initial coordinates, appendCoord 0 has only the final coordinate t.
euclideanProduct 0 E is the image of F under that map.

background_notes.justification: A nonempty subset of a singleton contains its unique element and hence equals the singleton. Thus every (x,t) in F has the unique empty-coordinate x and t∈I; its appended vector has only coordinate t. Conversely, for every t∈I that unique x belongs to E and supplies a preimage. This proves both image inclusions.
